title: Chapter 4 Quiz 5
description: Sorting by swapping neighbours that are out of order.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What does **bubble sort** do?
options: Swaps neighbours in the wrong order
Picks the smallest value each time
questions.explanation: Neighbouring pairs are compared and swapped when needed. Watch out: picking the smallest value is selection sort.

questions.question: In ascending bubble sort, when are two neighbours swapped?
options: When the left one is greater
When the left one is smaller
questions.explanation: array[j] > array[j+1] means the pair is in the wrong order. Watch out: equal values need no swap.

questions.question: Complete the bubble sort of 5 elements.
questions.code:
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    For j From 1 To {{1}} Do
        If array[j] {{2}} array[j + 1] Then
            temp ← array[j]
            array[j] ← array[j + 1]
            array[j + 1] ← temp
        EndIf
    EndFor
EndFor
questions.explanation: The inner loop stops at 5 - i because the end is already sorted. We swap when the left is greater.

questions.question: Sort [5, 1, 4, 2, 8] with bubble sort. Give the array after each pass.
questions.explanation: Each pass moves the largest remaining value to the right end. Watch out: after pass 1 the array is not sorted yet, only the last cell is final.

questions.question: After the first pass of bubble sort, where is the largest element?
questions.explanation: The big value bubbles up to the last position.

questions.question: How many comparisons does the first pass of bubble sort make on 5 elements?
questions.explanation: A pass compares pairs (1,2), (2,3), (3,4), (4,5): 4 comparisons. Watch out: 5 elements give 4 pairs.

questions.question: How many comparisons does the whole bubble sort make on 5 elements, with the loop above?
questions.explanation: The passes compare 4, 3, 2 and 1 pairs: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10. Watch out: the inner loop gets shorter on every pass.

questions.question: Bubble sort is rarely used in production.
questions.explanation: It is simple and educational, but slow: O(n²).

questions.question: This bubble sort works on 5 elements. One line is wrong because it reads outside the array. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    For j From 1 To 5 Do
        If array[j] > array[j + 1] Then
            Swap(array[j], array[j + 1])
        EndIf
    EndFor
EndFor
options: For j From 1 To 5 + i Do
For j From 1 To 5 - i Do
For j From 2 To 5 - i Do
For j From 1 To 4 + i Do
questions.explanation: When j = 5, array[j + 1] is array[6], which does not exist. Watch out: the bound 5 - i is also shorter, since the end is already sorted.

questions.question: This should sort in ascending order. One line has an error.
questions.code:
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    For j From 1 To 5 - i Do
        If array[j] < array[j + 1] Then
            Swap(array[j], array[j + 1])
        EndIf
    EndFor
EndFor
questions.explanation: We swap when the left value is greater. Watch out: with < the code sorts in descending order.
